newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE IN QUIET TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE IN QUIET TRADE.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted softer in quiet trade on Wednesday despite a drop in the level of liquidity.
"The market is sort of quietish at the moment. (Central) Reserve Bank figures show a drop in liquidity due to decreased volumes of treasury bill maturities," a dealer said.
He said discount houses were still taking up treasury bills at 19.36 percent from the central bank with 30, 60 and 90-day NCDs falling to 19.75 percent from 21 percent on Tuesday.

Bankers acceptances with maturity of 30 days were quoted at 19.50 percent while the 60 and 90-day bills were at 19.75 percent. This compared with a buying rate of 20 percent for BAs across the board the previous day.
Call money, however, added one percent point to 19 percent and Reserve Bank figures showed a pre-settlement market surplus of Z$97 million, down from Z$770 million previously.
